serviceTypes.name: Day care centre
serviceTypes.description: A centre where she spends the day with meals, activities and care, while you work.

serviceTypes.name: Day care for dementia
serviceTypes.description: Day care for people living with dementia, at selected centres.

serviceTypes.name: Transport to and from day care
serviceTypes.description: Pick-up and drop-off between home and the centre.

serviceTypes.name: Help with washing and dressing at home
serviceTypes.description: A trained care worker comes home to help with washing, dressing, eating and toileting.

serviceTypes.name: Nurse visits at home
serviceTypes.description: A nurse visits to handle wounds, tubes, injections or medicines.

serviceTypes.name: Therapy at home
serviceTypes.description: Physiotherapy, occupational or speech therapy at home, to help her regain everyday abilities.

serviceTypes.name: Escort to appointments
serviceTypes.description: Transport to medical appointments, with someone to go with her.

serviceTypes.name: Meals delivered
serviceTypes.description: Meals delivered to her home when she can't buy or prepare her own.

serviceTypes.name: A break for you
serviceTypes.description: Full-time care at a nursing home for at least 7 days, so you can rest.

serviceTypes.name: Activities and company nearby
serviceTypes.description: A neighbourhood centre for activities, exercise and befriending.

serviceTypes.name: Short-term carer after discharge
serviceTypes.description: A carer at home for up to 2 weeks after discharge. Only the ward's medical social worker can refer her, while she is in hospital.

serviceTypes.name: Nursing home
serviceTypes.description: Full-time care in a home, for when care at home isn't enough.

needRules.reasonText: Ask the ward's medical social worker before she leaves. This help can only be requested while she is in hospital.
Staff trained in dementia care look after her during the day.
Someone is with her while you're at work.
A trained carer helps with daily care at home.
Therapy helps her get back her strength and movement.
Someone gets her safely to clinic visits.
Regular meals arrive at her door.
You need a break too. This gives you one.
Company and activities close to home.
A nurse handles the medical care at home.

branches.firstContact: The medical social worker on her ward
askList: When is she likely to be discharged?
Can you refer her for short-term help at home, like the Interim Caregiver Service or a Hospital-to-Home programme?
Will she get the single care assessment, and who arranges it?
Which services can you refer her to from here?
Can she be assessed for the Home Caregiving Grant?
Who do I call if things go wrong in the first week at home?
timelineNotes: The Interim Caregiver Service gives up to 2 weeks of help at home. Hospital-to-Home programmes can support her for up to 2 months.
The Interim Caregiver Service can only be requested while she is still in hospital.

branches.firstContact: A polyclinic doctor or an AIC Link
askList: Can you assess what care she needs now?
Can you refer her for the services in this plan?
Which subsidy range is she in, and how do we confirm it?
Is there a waiting list, and what can we use until then?

branches.firstContact: An AIC Link, or the AIC hotline on 1800-650-6060
askList: Can you help us arrange respite care? A doctor's referral is needed about 4 weeks before.
Can she go to day care while I work or rest?
What caregiver support or training is there near us?
Am I likely to qualify for the Home Caregiving Grant or the Caregivers Training Grant?
What will we pay each month after subsidy?
Can CareShield Life, MediSave Care or ElderFund payouts go straight to you?
What isn't included in the monthly fee?
timelineNotes: Median wait for a nursing home bed: about 1 month for general care needs, about 2–4 months for psychiatric care needs. MOH, Aug 2024.

dementiaFlag.note: Nursing home beds for psychiatric care needs take longer to get. The median wait is about 2–4 months, against about 1 month for general care (MOH, Aug 2024).

prices.derived: High: NTUC Health $1,606 a month ÷ 21.7 weekdays.

tiers.avRule: No household income and home Annual Value at or below $21,000 also falls here.
No household income and home Annual Value above $21,000 also falls here.

grantRules.name: Home Caregiving Grant
grantRules.otherConditions: Not living in a nursing home or other residential facility. Households owning more than one property get $200. Needs a Functional Assessment Report from an approved assessor, then an online application on AIC's eFASS.

grantRules.name: MediSave Care
grantRules.otherConditions: Withdraw up to $200 a month from MediSave. The amount depends on the MediSave balance, not income.

grantRules.name: CareShield Life payout
grantRules.otherConditions: For people covered by CareShield Life who need help with 3 or more daily activities. $689 a month is the 2026 claim amount; it is fixed by the year of the first claim.

grantRules.name: ElderFund
grantRules.otherConditions: For Singapore Citizens with severe disability and low income and MediSave balance. Up to $250 a month; individual amounts can be lower. The income and MediSave limits aren't encoded here, so confirm with AIC.

grantRules.name: Helper levy concession
grantRules.amountMeaning: Monthly levy payable with the concession (instead of $300).
grantRules.otherConditions: For a household with a live-in migrant domestic worker and a Singapore Citizen aged 67 or over, or a person a doctor certifies as needing help with at least 1 daily activity.

grantRules.name: Caregivers Training Grant
grantRules.amountMeaning: $400, then $200 a year (up to $400 at a time) for approved courses. She must be 65 or older, or have a disability.
grantRules.otherConditions: For caregivers of a Singapore Citizen or PR aged 65 or over, or with a disability, taking approved courses.

alwaysBring: Your NRIC (as the person arranging care)
The hospital discharge summary or doctor's memo, if any
A list of her current medicines
A rough idea of the monthly income of everyone living at her NRIC address (subsidies are means-tested on it)

routes.firstContact: Her doctor at the hospital or polyclinic, or an AIC Link
steps: Ask the doctor to submit an online application for the service.
Or visit an AIC Link and they will help you apply.
Subsidies are means-tested on household income per person.
extraDocuments: The doctor's referral or the application made by the hospital or polyclinic

routes.firstContact: The medical social worker on her ward
steps: Ask before she is discharged. Only the ward's medical social worker can refer her.

routes.firstContact: The ward's medical social worker, or her polyclinic doctor
steps: A hospital, polyclinic or medical social worker refers her after an assessment finds she can't be cared for at home.
extraDocuments: The referral from the hospital or polyclinic

routes.firstContact: Her doctor, with help from an AIC Link
steps: A hospital, polyclinic or GP doctor refers her. An AIC Link can help with the application.
Apply about 4 weeks before. Each stay is at least 7 days, up to 30 days a year.
Call or walk in and ask what's available.
Get a Functional Assessment Report from an approved doctor, nurse or therapist.
Apply online on AIC's eFASS with Singpass.

extraDocuments: A doctor's certification of the help she needs and AIC's recommendation letter (if applying because of daily activities)
